scope: the Allegrex executable of the pinned USA disc
provenance: No toolchain has been qualified yet. The PS2 siblings could not use a modern GCC for the R5900 either, and they solved it by measuring the register mode of the target; the Allegrex case has to be measured the same way. Waves 2 and 3 measured it, and the measurement discriminates: the rule of the retail code is the rule of a configuration, and the configuration is now named.

measured.note: What the code of the retail executable says about the compiler that built it. Measured by tools/code_idioms.py; the numbers are in config/boot/idioms.json. These are properties of the compiler configuration, not of the code.
measured.stack_slot_evidence: 93 of the 93 frame sizes the code opens are multiples of 16 bytes.
measured.prologue_rule: The callee-saved registers are pushed first, at the bottom of a save area aligned on sixteen bytes, and $ra is pushed last, just above them: the number of slots between the frame and the saved $ra is 1 in 1524 bodies, 2 in 3033, 3 in 2133 and 4 in 6798.
measured.prologue_rule_cause: MIPS_STACK_ALIGN (mips.h:2876) aligns the stack on 8 bytes for o32, o64 and eabi, and on 16 for n32 and n64; UNITS_PER_WORD (mips.h:1490) is 4 in o32. The retail rule - slots of four bytes in a save area aligned on sixteen - is therefore a property of the TARGET CONFIGURATION, not of the compiler version. A GCC 3.3 in n32 gives the alignment but eight-byte slots; a GCC 3.3 in o32 gives four-byte slots and eight-byte frames; only the PlayStation 2 EE configuration gives both, and it does.
measured.position_independence_evidence: the code contains no lui $gp, no addiu $gp and no load from $gp: every global is reached through an absolute address. The module is therefore linked at a fixed address, and .text starts at 0x00000000.
measured.debug_c_evidence: CORRECTED. The option is -mdebugc (TARGET_DEBUG_C_MODE) and it is OFF by default (MASK_DEBUG_C 0, mips.h:247). GCC 3.3.6 emits sltu rX,rX,1 four times in the equality probe WITH OR WITHOUT the option, exactly as the ee-gcc 2.95.2 probe does. The retail code has none, zero out of 3528 sltu, so its absence is a property of THE CODE and not evidence about the compiler. The earlier reading of this as a discriminator was wrong, and it is withdrawn.
measured.branch_likely_evidence: The retail code holds 6941 branch-likely instructions: beql, bnel, blezl, bgtzl, bltzl and bgezl. A compiler of the 2.95 line emits NO branch-likely at all, and a compiler of the 3.x line emits them. The 2.95.2 witnesses of wave 4 were measured and never produce one, while the 3.3.6 produces bnel. This measurement needs no compiler at all: it is a property of the code, and it places the retail build on the 3.x line or later, and excludes the 2.95 line.
measured.one_return_evidence: the review of wave 1 found exactly one jr $ra per body, at end - 8, with its delay slot at end - 4.
measured.distance_frame_to_save_of_ra: from 1 to 15 instructions, the mode at 1: the callee-saved registers are usually pushed before the return address.
measured.library: the strcmp of the retail code at 0x00245504 is the newlib 1.15 size variant, the one selected by PREFER_SIZE_OVER_SPEED: thirteen instruction slots, no frame, four delay slots all filled with useful code, a signed byte comparison and an unsigned difference, with no masking at all. The library was therefore built with -Os, or with PREFER_SIZE_OVER_SPEED defined.

candidates.kind: PlayStation 2 Emotion Engine cross compiler, GCC 2.95.2, o32 ABI with 64-bit registers
candidates.provenance: The ee-gcc 2.9-ee-991111 of the sibling PlayStation 2 projects, rebuilt and re-measured by wave 3.
candidates.measured_cause: it is the only compiler measured that reproduces BOTH properties of the retail code: the prologue rule ($ra at frame - 16 in 26 of 26 bodies, 16-byte frames) and the form of the strcmp (13 slots, lb and lbu, no masking).
candidates.residual_difference: its strcmp uses beql where the retail code uses bnel. That is the one difference left, and it is what decides between the 2.95 line and the 3.x line.
candidates.regression_control: the population of 13 495 bodies for the prologue, and the exact newlib 1.15 source for the strcmp.

candidates.provenance: Built by wave 3 from the sources of the community port, with binutils 2.25.1, gmp 4.3.2, mpfr 2.4.2, mpc 0.8.1 and the newlib 1.15.0 headers. The recipe is reproducible: work/H1/build.md.
candidates.measured_cause: in every one of the nine ABI and ISA configurations it was built for, it fails the prologue rule: o32 and eabi give four-byte slots and eight-byte frames, n32 gives the alignment but eight-byte slots. The strcmp is 17 slots at -Os and 22 at -O2, against the 13 of the retail code.
candidates.regression_control: the corpus of 180 bodies for the prologue, and the exact newlib source for the strcmp.

candidates.provenance: The PSPSDK 0.15.0 of ps2dev, with the psp-gcc 8.2.0 it ships. Obtained: a native Windows build.
candidates.measured_cause: it puts $ra at frame_size - 4 in 15 of 15 bodies, and does not always allocate a frame of a multiple of 16 (15 of 20). The retail rule is a spread over 1 to 4 slots below $ra, and 93 of 93 frames are multiples of 16.
candidates.regression_control: the strcmp it compiles has 11 slots at -Os and 19 at -O2, against the 13 of the retail code, and it masks with andi where the retail code does not mask at all.

candidates.provenance: pspdev/gcc, the port of a current GCC to the Allegrex, branch allegrex-v15.2.0, commit 1a339979, built by psptoolchain-allegrex. Obtained: the pspdev image.
candidates.measured_cause: same as the 8.2: $ra at frame_size - 4 in 16 of 16 bodies, and 13 of 20 frames a multiple of 16.
candidates.regression_control: the strcmp it compiles has 11 slots at -Os and 15 at -O2, against the 13 of the retail code.

candidates.kind: Allegrex MIPS cross compiler, GCC 3.3 lineage, the PSPSDK toolchain
candidates.provenance: The toolchain the PSP SDK shipped. The community port BRS-PSP-Research-Initiative/Psptoolchain-Allegrex-3.3 names the sources: sourceware git branch releases/gcc-3.3, described as the version Sony built the PSP toolchain off of; binutils 2.25.1; newlib-cygwin 1.15.0.
candidates.obstacle: the community port does not carry the Allegrex machine description in an applicable form, with 28 patch rejects. Wave 3 built the same GCC 3.3.6 from the same sources for mips-elf, and it works; the missing part is the machine description alone.
candidates.caveat: the community port brings in the modern Allegrex support, so a compiler rebuilt through it would follow the modern convention. It would falsify the fidelity of the port, not the hypothesis.

candidates.provenance: pspdev/clang-psp, a backend that was frozen in 2020.
candidates.measured_cause: a 2020 backend cannot be the compiler of a 2005 game, and the retail prologue rule is not one of the shapes a modern clang produces.

candidates.provenance: The Allegrex static-recompilation toolkits: sp00nznet/psprecomp, wizardengineer/psprecomp and the psprism toolchain of anthonyhfm/psprism.
candidates.notes: These recompile rather than decompile. They are the right family of tools for the portability goal, and the wrong tool for the matching goal; they are listed because the project may deliver both, and because the recompilation route is what makes the game playable without the hardware.

hypotheses.statement: The retail build is a GCC of the 3.x line, Allegrex target, built without the debug-C mode, with the library compiled for size.
hypotheses.verdict: CONFIRMED on the line, and the clause about the debug-C mode is WITHDRAWN. The 6941 branch-likely instructions of the retail code place it on the 3.x line: the 2.95 line emits none. The clause about the debug-C mode is withdrawn, because the option is off by default and the idiom is emitted with or without it.

hypotheses.statement: The retail build is a GCC of the 2.95 line, in the PlayStation 2 EE configuration.
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED. A GCC 3.3.6 was built in the PlayStation 2 EE configuration - a new target, mips64r5900el-unknown-elf, ported from the SDK 2.95.2 elf5900.h - and it replays neither the prologue rule nor the form of the strcmp. And the 2.95.2 witnesses themselves are now excluded by the branch-likely measurement, which needs no compiler: they never emit bnel, and the retail code holds 3089 of them.

hypotheses.statement: The retail build is a GCC of the 3.x line, in the configuration of the PSPSDK's Allegrex target: o32 words, so four-byte save slots, and a stack aligned on sixteen bytes.
hypotheses.verdict: OPEN, and it is now the only configuration left standing. The two properties are measured on the retail code: 14655 of the 14656 frame openings are a multiple of 16, and the save area is four bytes wide, which is o32. No stock GCC configuration has both: o32 aligns the stack on 8 and saves in 4 bytes, n32 aligns on 16 and saves in 8. A stock GCC 3.3.6 in the PlayStation 2 EE configuration gives the alignment but eight-byte slots; with -mgp32 it gives the four-byte slots. The PSPSDK's Allegrex target is a custom one that has both, and it is the configuration the retail code was built with.
hypotheses.measured_cause: MIPS_STACK_ALIGN (mips.h:2876) is 8 for o32, o64 and eabi, and 16 for n32 and n64; UNITS_PER_WORD (mips.h:1490) is 4 in o32. The retail rule is the combination of an alignment of 16 with words of 4, which stock GCC does not offer.
hypotheses.falsified_if: a GCC 3.3.6 whose MIPS_STACK_ALIGN is 16 and whose words are 4 does not reproduce the prologue rule of the retail code on a corpus, with the saved $ra in the same places.

notes: The measurement is the advance; the qualification is not. What the project holds is a discriminator that separates the candidates without guessing, a recipe to build each of them, and a name for the configuration the retail code was built with. The branch-likely count is the decisive one and it is published in config/boot/idioms.json, with the tool that measures it in tools/code_idioms.py. See work/TOOLCHAIN/shape.tsv, work/H1/shape.tsv and work/H2/shape.tsv for the tables, work/H1/build.md and work/H2/build.md for the recipes.
